reference.source: OMIM / GeneReviews (NCBI) and standard mitochondrial disease references
clinicalPearls: Multisystem mitochondrial disorder of infancy caused by a single large-scale deletion of mitochondrial DNA, usually sporadic
Cardinal features are a transfusion-dependent sideroblastic anaemia and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
Bone marrow characteristically shows ring sideroblasts and prominent vacuolisation of erythroid and myeloid precursors
Cytopenias may extend beyond anaemia to neutropenia and thrombocytopenia
Lactic acidosis and other metabolic derangements reflect impaired oxidative phosphorylation
The pancreatic insufficiency causes malabsorption, failure to thrive and steatorrhoea, and hepatic and renal tubular dysfunction may occur
Survivors of the haematological phase may later develop the features of Kearns-Sayre syndrome
Diagnosis is confirmed by demonstrating a single large-scale mitochondrial DNA deletion, with supportive marrow and biochemical findings
reference.pathophysiology: Pearson syndrome is caused by a single large-scale deletion of mitochondrial DNA, typically arising sporadically. Loss of genes encoding oxidative phosphorylation subunits and mitochondrial transfer RNAs impairs cellular energy production and disrupts mitochondrial iron handling, producing sideroblastic anaemia with ring sideroblasts. High-turnover tissues such as the bone marrow and exocrine pancreas are severely affected. The heteroplasmic burden of deleted genomes can shift with time, so surviving children may transition toward a Kearns-Sayre phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Other mitochondrial cytopathies including Kearns-Sayre syndrome
additionalInvestigations: Full blood count and blood film showing sideroblastic anaemia and cytopenias
Bone marrow examination for ring sideroblasts and vacuolated precursors
Molecular analysis for a single large-scale mitochondrial DNA deletion
Blood lactate and metabolic screen for lactic acidosis
Faecal elastase and assessment of exocrine pancreatic function
Hepatic and renal tubular function tests
redFlags: Multiorgan failure involving liver and kidney
Symptomatic pancytopenia requiring intensive transfusion support
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is poor, with high mortality in infancy from metabolic crises, infection and marrow failure. The anaemia may improve spontaneously in children who survive, but these survivors are at risk of progressing to Kearns-Sayre syndrome; management is supportive and multidisciplinary.
pitfalls: Mistaking the marrow findings for a primary haematological malignancy or Shwachman-Diamond syndrome
Overlooking the underlying mitochondrial aetiology in an infant with refractory anaemia
Failing to anticipate metabolic decompensation during intercurrent illness
Not recognising possible later evolution into Kearns-Sayre syndrome
